vopros: I run a small service business in Los Angeles and customers keep haggling on price. Who in LA can help me with that?

vyzhimka.tekst:
For a small service business, I’d look for help in **two areas**: setting a defensible price and training you to handle objections without automatically discounting.

### Good Los Angeles options

1. **PACE Business Development Center** — free/low-cost small-business counseling  
   They offer help with pricing strategies, sales, financial planning, and business growth. They have offices in Downtown LA, Hollywood, and El Monte.  
   - Downtown: **213-353-9400**  
   - Hollywood: **213-989-3158**  
   Website: [pacela.org/our-work/business](https://pacela.org/our-work/business/)

2. **LA BusinessSource Centers** — no-cost consulting for LA businesses  
   These City of Los Angeles-supported centers provide one-on-one consulting, marketing advice, market assessments, and other business support. CRCD operates locations serving South and Southeast LA.  
   - **323-450-7226**  
   Website: [coalitionrcd.org/business-assistance](https://coalitionrcd.org/business-assistance/)

3. **Los Angeles Urban League Entrepreneurship Center** — pricing and sales coaching  
   Their counselors specifically cover **pricing strategies for products and services**, sales coaching, budgeting, and financial analysis.  
   Website: [laul.org](https://laul.org/)

4. **LA PI.N. Negotiation Services** — private negotiation coaching  
   Useful if the main issue is what to say when customers push back. They offer one-on-one negotiation coaching, preparation, and business negotiation advice.  
   Website: [lapinnegotiationservices.com](https://lapinnegotiationservices.com/negotiation-services-los-angeles/)

5. **The Pricing Lady** — specialized service-business pricing consultant  
   This is a more targeted private option for restructuring offers, communicating value, and creating pricing rules that reduce ad hoc discounting.  
   Website: [thepricinglady.com](https://thepricinglady.com/)

6. **Local sales/business coaches**  
   A sales coach can role-play price objections and help you build a repeatable script. For example, LA-area business coaches advertise work on pricing, sales strategy, and revenue growth. Vet them carefully and ask for references from businesses similar to yours.

### What to ask for specifically

When contacting someone, say:

> “I run a service business in Los Angeles. Customers regularly ask for discounts, and I want help reviewing my pricing, packaging my services into good/better/best options, and developing scripts for price objections.”

You probably don’t need “negotiation” in the formal corporate sense. You need:

- Clear value-based pricing
- A minimum acceptable price
- Packages or tiers instead of open-ended discounts
- A policy for when discounts are allowed
- Scripts for responses such as:  
  **“I understand you’re comparing prices. Our price reflects [specific outcome/quality/speed]. I can offer a smaller package at $X, but I don’t reduce the price for the same scope.”**

I’d start with **PACE or BusinessSource for free guidance**, then hire a private pricing or sales consultant if you need deeper help.
